record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Does there exist an aperiodic infinite word whose factors all have FG-palindromic length bounded by a constant?

evidence.quote: Does an aperiodic infinite word exists such that the FG-palindromic lengths of its factors are bounded by a constant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the free monoid of finite words over A. A finite word w ∈ A* is called a palindrome if it equals its reversal. Embed A* into the free group F(A) generated by A. For a finite word w ∈ A*, define the FG-palindromic length of w to be the least integer k ≥ 0 such that w, viewed as an element of the free group F(A), can be written as a product of k palindromes (each palindrome being an element of A* that reads the same forwards and backwards), where the equality is taken in F(A) (so cancellations between the palindromic factors are allowed). 

An infinite word u ∈ A^ℕ is called periodic if u = v^ω for some finite nonempty word v, and aperiodic otherwise. A factor of u is any finite contiguous subword of u.

Question: Does there exist an aperiodic infinite word u over some finite alphabet A such that the set {FG-palindromic length of f : f is a factor of u} is bounded by a constant?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for ordinary (free monoid) palindromic length — whether every aperiodic infinite word has factors of unbounded palindromic length — was conjectured by Frid, Puzynina, and Zamboni in 2013 and remains open in general (proved only for special classes such as k-power-free or Sturmian words). The free-group (FG) variant of the palindromic length was introduced and studied by Saarela and others around 2017; the boundedness question for aperiodic infinite words in the FG-setting does not appear to have been resolved in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic Length in Free Monoids and Free Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and studies the FG-palindromic length, the palindromic length of a word interpreted in the free group.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of FG-palindromic length is defined and studied; the question of whether aperiodic infinite words can have factors of bounded FG-palindromic length is posed.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic length and reduction of powers
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishing unboundedness of palindromic length for k-power-free aperiodic words; the general conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The (ordinary) palindromic length conjecture for aperiodic words is open in general, with only partial results.
